A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
a 3D DRAMA design with re-architectured 2D DRAM dies can achieve up to a 3x improvement in performance and a 2x improvement in power compared to 2D DRAMA designs.
the 3rd dimension of DRAM stacking is an effective solution for future main memory design, and it is essential to re-architect the 2D dies to achieve full benefits of 3D stacking.
3D DRAMS are not a silver bullet for future memory architectures.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the 3rd dimension is not a panacea for future DRAM designs; instead, 3D die stacking requires a re-thinking of the entire DRAM design and system architecture.
the 3rd dimension of die stacking can only be exploited effectively when the 2D DRAM dies are redesigned and when the system is aware of the new DRAM architecture.
the 3-dimensional integration of DRAMs is a powerful technology, but it is not a magic bullet for solving the power, area, or timing problems of 2D DRAMs.
